rationale: The functional-food review discusses omega-3 fatty acids and study outcomes across conditions. It supplies no exposure to raw fig or estimate of drooling severity in Parkinson disease.
The mini-review compares microbiota profiles across weight groups and Parkinson disease. Its dietary and figure references provide no fig-specific exposure or drooling result.
The genetic association study addresses sleep traits and Parkinson disease susceptibility. Its outcome estimates are about risk, without a raw fig or graded drooling contrast.
The reporting-system study examines suspected drug-induced movement disorders. Its adverse-event comparisons provide no raw-fig intake or Parkinson drooling assessment.
This review inventories Parkinson scales and earlier outcome measures. References to saliva and drooling are item or instrument context, with no raw fig intervention.
The six-cohort model uses a saliva and drooling item to predict initiation of dopaminergic medication. The fitted association is separate from a change in symptom severity due to fig.

The Irish qualitative study explores social experience in Parkinson disease. Drooling appears among symptoms contributing to particular contexts. No preparation-specific dietary comparison was reported.

The 2,166 bounded SGIM members separate unrelated acute clinical presentations, dry mouth, a photography label and a poetry term from Parkinson reports. No original member jointly treats raw fig and Parkinson drooling.
The clinic article describes interdisciplinary gastrointestinal care, swallowing and drooling as referral or assessment contexts. It does not estimate a raw-fig response.
The case report describes inherited VAC14-related neurological disease in siblings and a related literature review. There is no food intervention or Parkinson drooling estimate.
Autonomic dysfunction is described from prior research. The review's prevalence and measurement discussions provide no primary raw-fig drooling comparison.
The case report concerns deep brain stimulation for a SERAC1-related disorder. Clinical treatment and outcomes give no raw fig exposure or comparable drooling measure.
Oral clinical findings serve as indicators of broader conditions in a dental review. The listed oral and systemic features supply no raw-fig or Parkinson drooling intervention.
The article groups Parkinson disease by dysautonomia characteristics and expression profiles. Composite symptoms and laboratory signals give no culinary attribution or raw-fig drooling response.
The Iranian registry reports an association between male gender and drooling. It does not measure fig ingestion or a change attributable to food.
The model study reports synaptic and connectivity findings and depressive behavior in mice. It supplies no raw fig exposure or measured Parkinson drooling outcome.
The article discusses cardiovascular autonomic disorders and management in synucleinopathies. Postural circulatory endpoints are distinct from raw fig or drooling severity.
The original analysis concerns rare PANK2-associated neurodegeneration. Its genetic and clinical comparisons give no raw-fig response or dietary drooling measure.
The clinical multicenter registry describes disease features and demographics in India. The observed symptom distributions give no raw fig or causal dietary contrast.
The regional review pools nonmotor symptoms in South Asian Parkinson disease. Prevalence and scale comparisons provide no tested fig effect.
The clinical case and rare variant review describe neurological presentations. Their outcomes do not identify a raw fig exposure or separately measured food-related drooling.
The multicohort model predicts cognitive impairment. The observed predictors and aggregate instruments do not give a fig or drooling treatment result.
The review compares vitamin D measures in Bell's palsy, a distinct population and outcome. It supplies no raw fig treatment or Parkinson drooling effect.
INTENSO compares historical rehabilitation groups on composite outcomes. Its drooling mention is background rather than an ingredient exposure or a separate effect estimate.
The article validates composite approaches to progression and treatment-effect assessment. It does not test raw fig or isolate a dietary drooling result.
The early-onset case series reports biallelic PDE1B-associated movement disorder. The cases and outcomes provide no fig exposure or Parkinson drooling measure.
The multinational study links good ON-time with burden and treatment-related outcomes. It gives no standalone raw-fig or drooling treatment comparison.
The clinical sample compares perceived swallowing and barium-study physiology. Its oral-residue and airway outcomes do not measure raw-fig effects or standalone drooling severity.
The qualitative study records symptoms and burden in advanced Parkinson disease from patients and clinicians. Participants describe drooling, without a fig exposure or measured change.
Sialorrhea contributes to an upper gastrointestinal subscore with other items. The stage and longitudinal analyses give no independent estimate for consuming raw fig.
This oral-health review distinguishes reduced clearance, saliva and oral disease. Its general dietary discussion supplies no isolated fig or primary drooling comparison.
The evidence review and consensus model describe patient-important outcomes in early Parkinson disease. It does not test a fig exposure against drooling severity.
The study validates a grouped upper gastrointestinal score and compares it with specific salivation and swallowing items. This is cross-sectional measurement without dietary attribution.
The clinical update discusses autonomic disorders and their management. It gives no raw fig trial or fig-attributable change in Parkinson drooling.
The narrative review examines computational detection approaches for Parkinson disease. It gives no raw fig consumption or symptom-effect estimate.

Published Padua source members include unrelated saliva sampling, parotitis and esophageal motility. Figure notation is unrelated to fruit. Presentation 097 has no published body and remains a separate follow-up trail.
The review summarizes patient perspectives in early or prodromal Parkinson disease. It gives no fig-specific observation or measured dietary drooling effect.
The review connects Lewy body diseases and gastrointestinal observations. It supplies no isolated raw-fig exposure or graded drooling comparison.
The clinical guidance addresses hepatolenticular degeneration. Its food-related management and symptom context are outside the frozen fig and Parkinson comparison.
The original describes acute liver failure in Wilson disease and a rescue therapy. This case supplies no raw-fig or Parkinson drooling comparison.
